reviews.title: BINGE casting stopped working immediately after cancelling my subscription
reviews.text:
I’ve recently experienced a frustrating problem with BINGE that I have been unable to resolve.

Until recently, I could cast programmes from my iPad to my television without any difficulty.

On 28 October, I cancelled my subscription, with confirmation that I would retain access until 19 November. However, on the same day, casting stopped working.

The BINGE app initially connects to my television, which displays “Ready to cast”. But the moment I select a programme, it plays on my iPad instead, the casting icon disappears, and nothing plays on the television.

I’ve restarted my iPad, checked the relevant permissions and confirmed that other streaming services, including YouTube, cast perfectly well to the same television.

I can still watch BINGE on my iPad, so the subscription clearly continues to provide access. The problem appears to be specifically with BINGE’s casting functionality.

I cannot say whether this is related to cancelling my subscription, but the timing is certainly curious.

A paid streaming service should work reliably until the subscription expires. It’s disappointing to encounter this problem, particularly when everything was working correctly the previous day.

BINGE needs to investigate these technical issues and provide a more reliable streaming experience.

reviews.title: Needs improvement
reviews.text:
The recent changes to the Live TV experience have made the app much harder to use.

* Please consider reverting to the previous Live TV/channel surfing interface. The previous experience was much more intuitive and made it easy to browse channels while watching TV.
* Apple TV navigation is extremely frustrating. When trying to move up or down the list of channels, the focus frequently jumps across to the programme listings instead of remaining on the channel list. It becomes very difficult to simply scroll through channels and often takes several attempts to reach the desired channel.
* Channel surfing has become difficult. On both the Apple TV and iPhone apps, it is no longer easy to browse or switch between live channels while continuing to watch the current channel. Instead, you are taken back to the TV Guide, making channel surfing slow and cumbersome.
* The Live TV guide text is too small on Apple TV. Channel names and programme information are difficult to read from a normal viewing distance.
* Picture quality could be improved. CNN HD appears noticeably soft compared to overseas HD feeds, and CNBC is only available in standard definition, making on-screen text and graphics difficult to read.

Overall, I would strongly recommend reverting to the previous Live TV navigation and channel surfing experience, or introducing an option for users to choose between the old and new interface. The previous design was much easier and faster to use.

reviews.title: Binge Update Broke Apple TV Integration - Now Basically Unusable
reviews.text:
Since the recent refresh of the Binge app, it’s basically become unusable on Apple TV.

Before the update, I could launch my shows directly from the Continue Watching section in the Apple TV app, which is kind of the whole point when you’re juggling multiple series across platforms. Now, every time I try, I get: “There was a problem opening Binge. Please try again later.”

The frustrating part? The same shows play perfectly fine if I open them inside the Binge app itself. So it’s clearly not a playback issue, it’s the integration that’s broken. That convenience has just disappeared overnight.

I’ve already done all the standard troubleshooting (reinstalled the app twice, restarted Apple TV, etc.), and when I reached out for support, I was just told to repeat those same basic steps instead of any acknowledgement that this might be a known issue since the update.

At the moment, it completely defeats the purpose of using Apple TV as a central hub. If this isn’t fixed soon, it’s a pretty poor user experience for anyone relying on Continue Watching.

Really hoping this gets addressed quickly.

reviews.title: Horrible to use & will lock you into paying
reviews.text:
This is easily one of the worst streaming experiences I’ve ever had.

First, the technical issues are unacceptable. The audio constantly went out of sync. I spent time switching devices and troubleshooting because I assumed it was an issue on my end. After searching online, it turns out this has been a known Binge problem for a long time, and they still haven’t fixed it. 

Then comes the cancellation process, which feels deliberately designed to trap people. The working is confusing and misleading, clearly intended to make cancelling harder than it should be. It shouldn’t feel like you’re navigating a maze just to end a subscription. 

To make matters worse, the Hubbl platform itself barely functions properly. Pages fail to load, and I had to switch devices and refresh multiple times just to get through the cancellation steps. I tried to do this before I was charged again and the hubbl platform said there was an outage I couldn’t get in and didn’t have time to sit there and keep trying so I got charged for a whole month I’m just not going to use, because of an outage with the Hubbl platform.


A service that doesn’t work properly and then makes it difficult to cancel is unacceptable. Avoid if you value your time, patience and money,

reviews.title: Silly Design
reviews.text:
The app is unnecessarily tedious to sign into with the “stream motion”/Hubbl account. I can’t update my email address on that account because the app just goes around and around in circles.

If I’m watching a show it doesn’t say the name of the show anywhere unless I click out of it. 

I use the subscription that shows ads which the app doesn’t remember, as in, if I need to rewind the show for any reason I might rewind too far then have to watch 2-3 minutes of the same ads I just watched. Other streaming apps don’t do this. 

The content isn’t consistently appealing so I only subscribe from time to time.

The clunkiness of your app isn’t just a you problem. Many apps have something silly about them. Your IT department need to be treated like technicians and not gods. They’re just tools in human form and need to do their jobs for customer satisfaction properly.

Millennials did not invent avocado toast and as far as being the generation that’s so awesome at computing- look at how easy it is to rob a bank these days. All from the comfort of the criminals own house. 

Get these people working. They’re destroying everything.
